covenants.name: The Cave of Twisting Shadows
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Criamon, a covenant older than the Christian era, carved into a mountain and repeated on nine levels of regio about the Axis Magica. Its device is an eye with the sign of infinity for its pupil. Many Criamon return here as their lives end; the young are sent away to bring fresh insight back when they return for new riddles.

Its people are mostly dead. Hundreds of ghosts of covenfolk and magi live on in families led by their living members, the weakest no more than patches of darkness, which give the covenant its name; the ghosts of the past Primi teach in place of a library, and are stingy with it. The autocrat is Hera, a ghost Criamon himself bound to the place. The living covenfolk never see daylight, grow distorted with age and often die young; they eat the nutty fungi of the mushroom farms Muscaria laid out, and speak a Romansch found nowhere else.

Customs. Visitors are welcome to learn the Enigma, vouched for by another covenant so as not to breach the Code, but none goes above the first level unless asked to a ritual; their tutors mark each insight with a tattoo. The council rules by consensus, the wisest weighing most, and seekers are sometimes asked to sit in it. When a Primus nears Twilight, a magus of another House ritually kills her before the ghosts of the past Primi, and the magi enter a communal vision until one rises as the new Primus (on the ninth level, and with Enigmatic Wisdom 3 or more, as Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults has it).

Magi. Sanctuary of Ice names fifteen; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults gives the Central Clutch twelve living magi, so the twelve it can hold are resident here (A10): the Prima Muscaria, Circum Perfico, Darius, Echo, Gunther, Hagen, Latrunculus, Pellam, Phalene, Regina, Siobhan and Viscus. Fortuito travels; Esther is petrified and arguably a member. La, Prima and Praeco in Sanctuary of Ice, has since been ritually slain and is one of the spectral Primi. The covenant counts twenty-two members in theory; eight live in the mundane land about it and belong only in law.

covenants.summary:
One of the Order's first covenants of magi trained by different masters, founded in 771 by Italians, as its name shows, and now a loose league of autonomous chapters that is a covenant mostly in law. Half a century after its founding the motherhouse and its three greatest chapters each claimed to be the true covenant; they settled before the Tribunal could break them up, and the chapters meet in council each year at the Midsummer Fair. It has nine chapters now, five of them a single magus each. Its device is a web or snowflake of three hexagons.

The motherhouse in Bavaria stands where Highest Aspiration fell in the Sundering of Tremere. The Quaesitores were set to harvest that covenant's vis, the Bavarian Common, and divide it each year; the trade that grew round the distribution raised the Common's chapter until the old motherhouse became a chapter and the magi moved here. It is all but a house covenant of Guernicus, home to four quaesitores and two hoplites, built far larger than its people need so that the Tribunal can meet in it, and many rooms stand empty but in summer. In an emergency a March gathers here.

A chair is offered for the best use of its empty buildings. Two dozen Gifted children were born at once in Sicily five years ago, and the likeliest proposal is a school for them by collegial training, which the Quaesitores favour lest so many of one age and affinity unbalance a single House. Mircalla, a mother murdered here by a magus's grogs when she came for her stolen daughter, haunts it, immune to Hermetic magic, kind to ill-used apprentices and ruinous to dangerous experiments, so no magus here keeps an apprentice.

Magi of the motherhouse: Athena Alpina, Cato, Adrasteia and Kentigern, the quaesitores; Archmage Vincent of Criamon and Katrina of Bjornaer, the hoplites. Thirteen more live in the chapters, of whom the book names Mary and Rogitien of Rorschach, Archmage Pietro of Juno's Spire and Archmaga Jacinta of the Tower of Ashes; the rest are unnamed.

covenants.name: The Covenant Where Journeys End
covenants.summary:
A covenant of Houses Merinita and Bjornaer in a regio on Mont Joux, founded in 817. Lucia filia Merinita came seeking the temple of Jupiter, found it sacked, and turned on the faeries instead, discovering a vast regio tied to Bright Winter and ruled by the White Lady, a queen of illusion. She killed the queen, took her kingdom and hunted her servants for the vis in them, sparing a few souled half-breeds to tend the vis sources; a decade later her apprentice founded the covenant. Peonn's death cut the regio off for about five years, and when the way was found again it claimed the vis Peonn had guarded. Its name comes from an old habit of kidnapping travellers until they no longer wished to leave, curbed this past century. Its device is a ring of sharp circumflexes.

The regio copies the mountain: long, low houses of blue-white stone on terraces above vineyards, orchards and fields, almost everything warped by the aura to magical sight; the magi's laboratories are burrowed into the mountain's heart and kept at mundane warmth. It is bitterly cold, and its people, crops and beasts have adapted, with a body heat far below normal; the magi make charms against heat and cold, often in wedding rings, but give them to no outsider. Its 200 covenfolk are warped by the Aura of Ice; their children together are at best faeries, so 5 or 6 well-chosen mundanes must be kidnapped or won as spouses each year. Two laboratories are made for ice-distorted magi, and no Ignem can be studied in them.

Uninvited mundanes meet a slow but very hostile answer from a small turb trained against faeries, good javelin men, some with spears that flash-heat and then freeze deep snow over their victims. It trades crystals, vis-spent wine and crafted goods at the Fair or through Rorschach. Only Merinita and Bjornaer magi vote, and Yselt, the senior Merinita, may veto any policy; there is always at least one Bjornaer, whose nature magic opens its oldest wards.

covenants.summary:
The Longevity Project, in caves behind a waterfall on a minor Danube tributary. Before the Order a hereditary priesthood kept a "dead god" here: an eight-foot skeleton chained by magical iron to a slab, which bleeds and slowly grows flesh, which the priests peeled away lest it rise and take revenge, and which slows aging when eaten. Guernicus judged it a human-shaped magical creature outside the Code. Someone wiped out the converted priesthood in the Sundering and tried to break its chains; House Guernicus sealed the site, and the Grand Tribunal of 865 gave it to Sancia filia Sabrina, archmaga of Perdo Corpus, who founded the Project. Its device is a cartouche crossed by a waterfall, a ruby at its foot.

Bonisagus's longevity potions were first bettered by Sabrina filia Maura, third Primus of Bonisagus; progress has since slowed to nearly nothing, the last breakthrough being a formula that slows apparent aging, and the chief researcher is forever brewing for Hermetic notables. An eleventh-century Verditius founded a little lineage of hydraulic magi, who with Valnastium's Greek texts have built water and steam machines far beyond Europe's.

It has no surplus income, which galls its magi: the Tribunal ordered it to stop making goods from vis to sell. It has no Hermes Portal, its magi have been surveying sites as far as Africa and Persia, and several minor covenants of outlying Tribunals have proposed a formal alliance that would make them its outlet. At its Aegis feast a dwarf's statue is sent over the falls in a barrel; it vanishes and turns up on the riverbank up to 21 miles away, and the covenfolk hunt it all year. Few grogs; its covenfolk, many in the village at the foot of the falls, speak Latin among their many tongues, their distortions mostly Immunities.

Magi: Archmaga Philomena and Hubert of Bonisagus, Archmage Paxon and Balbina of Verditius, Sabastien of Tytalus and Cara of Bjornaer, with Ragoneda of Tytalus as a long-term, non-voting visitor.

covenants.name: Tarragon Vale
covenants.summary:
A covenant of metaphysical geographers and explorers, Hermetic pioneers of Arcadia and the land of spirits, whose great breakthrough was the Narrative Map, a device showing the structures under the shifting lands of the mystic realms. They held that faeries were only ways of meeting deeper forces that better tools let one ignore, which made them many enemies in House Merinita.

Its four magi and its covenfolk vanished twenty-two years ago, the Vanishing Away, and no one has found out why. Its charter makes no provision for its end, so the Quaesitores will not dissolve it without bodies, lest its magi come back from Arcadia demanding their back vis: they store its income, spending only on its Aegis and its Shrouded Glen, and no estate may be settled without proof of death. The heirs want the hoard; most Alpine magi hope the heirs multiply until each gets only a rook. A quarter of those born here once had Second Sight, and its Sighted grogs were a prized export; the gift has waned, and children brought here to be born no longer get it.

Cymena, a Redcap without the Gift whose grandparents came from here, lives at the site by no right but custom.

covenants.name: Valnastium
covenants.summary:
The domus magna of House Jerbiton, the Founder's family villa in a Dolomite valley, founded in law in 773 and in practice about 775. Its device is a griffin collared with olive. Primi once built palaces round the town's plaza; most are now homes of favoured servant families or public buildings, and the Primus lives in the little villa on the hill as the Founder did. Magi lodge in the town and keep their laboratories in the gardens, among the enchanted graves of Jerbiton magi; the gardens, which the Founder laid out, are kept with reverence: a magically flat lawn, snails and dormice for the table, beehives, and plants from far lands in magical climates. Each fashion of the House leaves a layer in the valley, gallery, museum, patron's court, embassy or Roman farm.

Members churn faster than at other old covenants. By tradition it has twenty or twenty-one, counting its chapters in Vienna, Constance, Saint Gallen and Geneva and its ties to covenants of other Tribunals, all joined by Hermes Portals, though only the council here may bar anyone from them; the valley itself has eleven residents. Four more chairs go to visiting specialists and guests, and the twenty-first, Bonisagus's chair, is a bursary of up to seven years for an exceptional young magus or a new spring covenant.

The House elects its Primus by hourly ballots, one vote a magus, with proxies witnessed by a Quaesitor and no binding campaign promises; a Steward, a resident the Primus appoints, runs the House between Primi (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 51, in place of Sanctuary of Ice's Secundi). Grogs serve in tent groups of eight, the contubernium from which, they say, "turb" comes. Its library, the finest in the Order for mundane research, invented the sloping shelf and trains librarians for other covenants.

Magi resident: Primus Andru, Constance, Sourdine, Sirocco, Grazia, Kalliope, Bronwyn and Angela; Carmine of Flambeau lives here as Andru's wife and a vouched-for specialist, not a member. The Larta of Sanctuary of Ice (Josephine, François and Chloe) are covenfolk here, not members of the House.

tribunals.name: The Greater Alps Tribunal
tribunals.summary:
The Order's Tribunal of the high mountains, from Savoy and Geneva in the west through the Swiss lands, Rhaetia and the Dolomites to Bavaria, Salzburg, Carinthia and the Austrian marches in the east. Three Founders' domus magnae lie in or beside it, and its culture is old, proud and self-consciously Roman: its magi think of themselves as a senate of the wealthy, dress in stola and toga at formal occasions, and hold themselves aloof from the rest of the Order.

A rich Tribunal that keeps itself rich by keeping itself small. Vis is plentiful because the covenants have limited their people to what their sources can bear: no new covenant has been allowed for centuries, and a magus votes only if his covenant has bought him a chair, pledging ten pawns of vis a year to his upkeep. Instead of new covenants the old ones keep chapters, lesser houses near useful resources, and trade them among themselves. The covenants live by trading services to one another (longevity potions, books, enchanted goods, beasts), so each has an interest in the peace, and war between covenants, which the Code calls disorder, is lawful but almost unthinkable.

There are about a hundred magi in seven public covenants, and they live long: about three are recruited every two years. The young find it hard to be their own masters here, so most are sent away after their Gauntlet to the frontier Tribunals, Hibernia, the Levant, Novgorod, and called back decades later if they have proved worth a chair. The Tribunal exports its trouble this way, and seeds covenants at the Order's edges.

Old grudges: an unofficial ill will toward House Tremere, dating from the Sundering and refreshed by the vampiric corruption, and a watch on the borders, where magi of the Rhine and Transylvania raid Alpine vis sources and the Bavarian Common. The Tribunal backs Novgorod against the Tremere.

The meeting. It meets every seven years, most often at the motherhouse of the Covenant of the Icy North in Bavaria, which every covenant but Sinews of Knowledge prefers to the Praeco's home, and which was built to hold it. The first business is the ostracism; the Quinquennial Games follow a meeting. The Wizard's Grimoire dates rulings of the Tribunal to 1165 and 1194, which puts the meetings in 1200, 1207 and 1214 and the next in 1221; the book gives no season, and autumn is taken here, as the Liberalia is forgone in a Tribunal's year and the Games, which follow it, fall in November. Informal and Quaesitorial tribunals meet at the Midsummer Fair each June.

Officers. The Praeco is the eldest magus: the book makes La, then Prima of Criamon, Praeco, but she has since been ritually slain and Muscaria is Prima, so the eldest living magus whose age is given, Constance of Valnastium, is taken as Praeco here. The chief Quaesitor is Athena Alpina of Guernicus, Cato her deputy; Archmage Pietro of Flambeau is the lictor, the hoplite who leads a Wizard's March and carries the judges' symbols at the meeting.
tribunals.meeting_place: The Covenant of the Icy North

rulings.title: Chairs and vagrancy
rulings.says: A magus votes at the Tribunal only if his covenant has bought him a chair: it declares a permanent vis source, has the Quaesitores assess it, and pledges ten pawns a year of it to his upkeep, at least a year before the meeting if he is to vote. The vis is not paid to anyone; the pledge shows the covenant will not poach from its neighbours. Vis distilled from an aura ("farming") does not count. A magus with no chair is a vagrant, a Low Crime, though a chair registered at any time protects him from its punishments. A chair belongs to the covenant, whose council fills it when its magus leaves.

rulings.title: The yearly pawn
rulings.says: Each covenant pays a pawn of vis a year to the senior members of Houses Guernicus and Mercere in the Tribunal. It began as a tradition and entered the Code; it was once a pawn for each magus.

rulings.title: Vis treaties
rulings.says: Gifts of vis exchanged so often between two covenants that both sides want the supply guaranteed are ratified as treaties and entered in the Code; they are delivered in Frustration Week. A treaty's income may pay for a chair, but vis owed away may not.

rulings.title: No new covenants
rulings.says: No new covenant may be founded unless it can show that, after its costs, it can spend ten pawns a year on each magus from sources no one else has claimed, and a pawn for the Quaesitores and Redcaps. None has been allowed for centuries; the Tribunal grows by chapters instead.

rulings.title: Ostracism
rulings.says: As the first business of each meeting every magus writes on a sherd the name of the magus he most despises, or leaves it blank. If at least one magus in four named the one with the most sherds, that magus must leave the Greater Alps before the second full moon, for twenty-one years, or be Marched. The exile ends the day before a Tribunal. An ostracised Praeco is replaced by the next eldest, with no second vote; an ostracised chief Quaesitor by his deputy. An ostracised magus may hand the sigils he carries, his own aside, to another magus.

rulings.title: Amaranth
rulings.says: All amaranth, the faerie flower that addicts magi, is to be destroyed. The traffic goes on, around Ingolstadt above all; the neighbouring Tribunals have not banned it, and the Grand Tribunal has never been asked.

rulings.title: Churches the Code protects
rulings.says: The city of Constance and the monasteries of the Great and Little Saint Bernard passes, vital to the Redcaps and favoured by House Jerbiton, are named in the Code as places where even minor violence is judged interference with the Church.

rulings.title: Flagrant spending
rulings.says: Covenants may not draw attention to themselves by making goods from vis to sell. The ruling was aimed at Sinews of Knowledge, which was ordered to stop its trade.

rulings.title: Pilate's ghost
rulings.says: No magus may harvest vis from the ghost of Pontius Pilate on Mount Pilatus. The meeting that made the ruling also sent its condolences to the sodales of the magi crushed by the avalanche that spoiled the first attempt.

rulings.title: The Bavarian Common
rulings.says: After the Sundering of Tremere destroyed the covenant of Highest Aspiration, several covenants raced to claim its resources. An emergency meeting gave its vis sources to the Quaesitores to harvest and divide among the covenants each year, and disbanded every rival chapter house in Bavaria but the Icy North's. The Common supports two chairs, for the quaesitor and the hoplite who keep it.

rulings.title: The estates of Tarragon Vale
rulings.says: No estate of Tarragon Vale's vanished magi may be settled without proof of their deaths; until then the Quaesitores keep the covenant's vis income, spending only what its Aegis and its Shrouded Glen need. The heirs have pressed the matter at a meeting, and the Quaesitores' position was upheld pending further evidence.

rulings.title: A sanctum a season
rulings.says: Snadstrich of Ex Miscellanea, of no covenant, was said to have moved her sanctum seven times in one year. The Tribunal ruled that a magus may not establish a new sanctum more than once a season (The Wizard's Grimoire).

rulings.title: Andru's pardon
rulings.says: A faerie lord took grogs and covenfolk of Valnastium to use as pieces in a great game of his; its magi rescued them, killing many faeries. Andru argued that every magus may defend his property, servants included, and that the rescue was self-defence; the Tribunal narrowly accepted it and pardoned him (The Wizard's Grimoire; Sanctuary of Ice calls it a just war on one of the faerie kings of Val Fanes, and gossip says Andru claimed a summer prince's crown in it).

rulings.title: Syrestis's fine
rulings.says: Syrestis of Bjornaer, visiting covenants of the Greater Alps, killed livestock and game in his animal shapes, harming his hosts' relations with their neighbours. Both the Rhine and the Greater Alps heard the case: the Rhine fined him three pawns, the Greater Alps ten. A quaesitor ruled that he must pay the Greater Alps, where the crimes were done, and owed the Rhine nothing (The Wizard's Grimoire).

secrets.text: Athena Alpina's even-handedness toward House Tremere, which her neighbours call blatant favouritism, may see her ostracised at the next meeting.

secrets.title: Why Cato came to the Alps
secrets.text: Cato was sent to the Alps partly to make sure that, if Athena Alpina goes, Adrasteia of Tytalus does not become chief Quaesitor.

secrets.title: The dragon under the Alps
secrets.text: A myth runs through the Alps that the mountains lie across the spine of a dragon so large it eats other dragons, and that widespread disorder would wake it. Few magi believe it wholeheartedly.

neighbours.name: The Greater Alps
neighbours.summary:
Europe's largest labyrinth: ranges of mountains cut by valleys that join into passes, the roads of settlement, war and trade. Those who hold the passes hold the land. The roads are mostly too steep for carts, so goods go by horse and mule, or by water: the lakes are crossroads, and the lake towns are some of the oldest and richest in the region, though the rivers run to rapids where they fall steeply. Wheat grows in the lower and warmer passes, rye in most places, and most mountain villages have as many mouths as their land can feed.

Nobles here build castles and towns in a frenzy, following the now-extinct Zähringers; the book puts some of the blame on the folly spirits, which lay their eggs in new buildings and breed paranoia in the castles they inhabit, so that many Alpine castles hold weak magic auras that suit magi. Most great lords are absentees, and lesser lords style themselves counts. Towns and lords band together in peace alliances (landfriedensbund).

neighbours.name: The Western Alps
neighbours.summary: From Savoy and the Jura to Lake Constance and Rhaetia: the Oberland plateau between the Jura and the Alps is the breadbasket, the most densely peopled land. The Little and Great Saint Bernard have been the great passes until now; around 1220 the Saint Gotthard opens a quicker road from the Italian trading cities to the north, and wealth begins to shift to the towns on the new route. Saint Gallen's lowland exports wheat, and the southern foothills grow Mediterranean crops. The Zähringers died out in 1217 with Berthold V, and their lands passed to the Kyburgs; Zurich and Lucerne are imperial cities, Berne the Emperor's since 1218.

neighbours.name: Bavaria
neighbours.summary: A broad plateau ringed and pierced by mountains, divided north and south by the Danube, whose valley and tributaries carry its trade and hold most of its people. Its wealth is trade, timber and farming; apart from Augsburg it has little mineral wealth, and its wilder parts are heavily forested. The ducal seat is Regensburg. The Wittelsbachs have ruled it since 1180 and gained the Rhenish Palatinate in 1214.

neighbours.name: The Eastern Marches
neighbours.summary: Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Salzburg: here the Alps grow harsher and split into three parallel ranges, east to west, each broken by passes, so the east is mountainous but easy to cross. The people live mostly in the eastern foothills, where the soil is richer, before the plains at the Tribunal's edge. The Brenner, in use since Roman times, is the great pass. The Babenbergs hold Austria and Styria; the duke's seat is Vienna, and the archbishop of Salzburg opposes him.

neighbours.name: The Axis Magica
neighbours.summary:
A mountainside honeycombed with looping tunnels, repeated on nine levels of regio, around a natural cave that runs through every level and opens into the Magic realm. House Criamon calls it the Axis Magica, the pivot about which the world's tides of magic wash, its world's navel and stairway to a finer existence. On the mundane level there is no sign of anyone living there. Things that turn up are mostly minor spirits rather than people, and the regio can be assailed from every direction from the Magic realm. Its highest level holds mind-traps, enchanted tunnels that catch airy spirits and abstractions.

Magic items kept long in the upper levels bleed their power into the Axis, so the covenant has none and no laboratory there can be bettered beyond +1; Enigmatic Wisdom rolls in the regio gain +2. The book numbers no level's aura: Magic 5 on the first, rising one a level to 13 on the ninth, is inferred (A10).

levels.name: The first level
levels.notes: Servants, stores, and the central cave as a mess hall; no visitor goes higher unless asked to a ritual.

levels.name: The eighth level
levels.notes: Where Sanctuary of Ice has a Primus slain and the past Primi summoned; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults moves the slaying to the ninth.

levels.name: The ninth level
levels.notes: The Hypostasis's threshold: no laboratory can work here; the Prima is slain and her successor chosen here (HoH:MC p. 55).

neighbours.name: The Motherhouse of the Icy North
neighbours.summary: Once the site of the covenant of Highest Aspiration, destroyed in the Sundering of Tremere. Its main building is a broad cone, tilted slightly north, with a stair winding round it to the top; it is older than its present use. A crenellated wall and watchtowers enclose the magi's and specialists' quarters, and a second wall the fairground and two great barracks used only in summer. Moderate slopes on every side, a road to the front gate, and about a visitor a day. A small town, which governs itself by a show of men's hands, rings the covenant. Magic aura 6.

neighbours.name: Mont Joux
neighbours.summary:
The highest peak in Europe, which later ages will call Mont Blanc: the tallest of a ridge of three. The Romans named it Mons Iovis for Jupiter Pennius, Peonn, the Celtic god of Alpine storms. No one has climbed it, and the priests say it is unlucky to try. In the eleventh century the blessed Bernard of Menthon chained the "demon" worshipped as Jupiter on the second peak, or drove it off a cliff, and that peak is now Mont Maudit, the Accursed Mountain.

Rock quartz, which needs great cold, and fluorite, which needs great heat, grow embedded in each other here, a contradiction of the natural order; the book gives them shape and material bonuses for enchanting, which stay in the book.

levels.name: The Covenant Where Journeys End
levels.enter: A gateway hidden by illusion under an icy lake on the mountain.
levels.notes: Bitterly cold, from below freezing at the summit to sharply cool at its edges. On the peak is a gate to Arcadia that lets travellers go far in minutes of mortal time and has no real guardian. The stat block gives Faerie 8; the text says 6 (A11).

neighbours.name: The Falls of Sinews of Knowledge
neighbours.summary: A minor waterfall on a tributary of the Danube in the Bavarian Alps, behind which runs a mostly artificial cave system whose plan, skilled vivisectionists say, is disturbingly like the blood vessels about a liver. A misplaced Great Bear is carved on the tunnel ceilings and enchanted to give light; no one knows its first purpose. An overshot wheel turns invisibly in the falls. A village lies at their foot, where merchants come in groups to trade. Magic 7 on the level of the magi's laboratories; deeper levels are higher and dangerously unstable.

neighbours.name: Tarragon Vale's Hill
neighbours.summary: A misty hilltop in Unterwalden. Tarragon Vale's long, barn-like stone hall stands three storeys high inside, mostly open, with rooms round the eaves; its many basements are sealed by the Quaesitores' wards, and its wooden outbuildings have rotted to compost. The Quaesitores keep up its Aegis and a Shrouded Glen. The book gives no aura; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: Valnastium
neighbours.summary:
A valley of the Dolomites, the family land of the Founder Jerbiton, whose ancestor was a Roman soldier settled here. Its entrance is hidden, its weather ruled by magic, its mouth barred by fortifications from the Schism War, and mountains overlook it on three sides, the river running through on the fourth. Almost a thousand people live in its villages and in the town round Jerbiton's villa, speaking a Rhaetian of their own; they call themselves the Ierbii. Its library is a true Temple of the Muses moved stone by stone from Greece, which the Founder brought for its aura.

Magic 3 over most of it; the church of Saint Cyprian has kept it from rising further, and much of the valley is Divine 2, rising to 6 at the church (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 53).

neighbours.name: The Church of Saint Cyprian
neighbours.summary: The valley's main church, raised with Hermetic magic and dedicated to Saint Cyprian, the magus who became a saint, though visitors take it for Cyprian of Carthage. Jerbiton knew closed communities draw diabolists, and his heirs have kept the sacraments regular here. Divine 6.

neighbours.name: The Aare Gorge
neighbours.summary: A deep crevasse near Meiringen, the lair of the Tatzelwurmli, a monstrous limbless land dragon, a kind of well worm. No covenant has claimed its vis, since none has shown it can harvest from the worm's lair.

neighbours.name: Baden
neighbours.summary: A town whose sulphur springs have been visited for their healing since Roman times: good for joints, heart and lungs, baldness and the heartsickness of failed love. Taking the cure, a month at a spa famed for the malady, lets a minor affliction be ignored for three years, though it heals nothing. Divine 3 (a town, DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Vindonissa
neighbours.summary: The ruins of the Roman fortress between Baden and Basel that guarded Helvetia from the Germans across the Rhine. Inside its fallen walls is Hapsburg castle, built by Bishop Werner of Strasbourg in the eleventh century, where a lesser scion of the Hapsburgs lives and his ancestors are buried.

neighbours.name: Botzberg
neighbours.summary:
Mons Vocetius, the field of the battle of AD 69 that ended Helvetian freedom from Rome. It is not haunted as such, but its remains can raise the ghosts of the fallen, who say priests, sounding like primitive magi, died in the battle; magi dig here now and then for those wizards' skulls.

Staying long, and sleeping there above all, rouses the field's spirits to fight the battle again, with any magi cast as the slain Roman priests. A survivor would know where his skull lies; every party that has tried has died and been dumped at the field's edge.

neighbours.name: The Cirque d'Annibal
neighbours.summary: A field near the Little Saint Bernard with a vast circle of ten rough monoliths, where Hannibal waited for his stragglers and held his council of war. Magi call it ill-omened, full perhaps of the spirits of those who died on the march from Carthage, angered by Rome's heirs; the wilder tales have its shadows fuse into a demon, part bronze, part man and mostly elephant.

neighbours.name: The Domleschg
neighbours.summary:
A valley of twenty-one castles in every state of use and ruin. Legend says fifteen druids lived here in the Order's early years and fought Diedne and her followers, believing a woman Archdruid would cut them off from their mysteries.

The victors raised a grove of oaks over the battlefield, each grown by magic from an acorn planted in a dead man's mouth. The motherhouse of the Icy North claims it as a source of Rego vis.

neighbours.name: The Pierres de Niton
neighbours.summary: Two large flat rocks in Lake Léman south-east of Geneva. Hermetic tales say House Diedne made human sacrifices on them, perhaps a garbled memory of Romans sacrificing to Neptune; the giant Gargantua is said to have thrown the larger into the lake, and to have dug the lake itself.

neighbours.name: Pfeffers
neighbours.summary: A Benedictine monastery founded in 713, by hot springs set in a crevice, into which patients are lowered on long ropes and left for a week at a time, food let down to them. Divine 5 at its church (a major monastery, DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Heiligenblut
neighbours.summary: A village named for the vial of Christ's blood in its church, brought by a Byzantine general who died of exposure here on campaign. A Tremere was Marched two centuries ago for trying to steal it. The book gives no aura; Divine 6 for the chapel of a most important relic (DE p. 418) is inferred.

neighbours.name: Lukerbad
neighbours.summary: The hottest springs in Europe, at Leuk, where a cure takes three weeks of ever longer bathing. Sabina, a powerful Flambeau maga, lived here last century and vanished; her laboratory has never been found, and some suspect her of unsavoury theurgy, living so near sulphurous wells.

neighbours.name: Martigny
neighbours.summary: Roman since AD 15, with a festival kept since then in which cows fight to be Queen of the Herd. Some magi think it once summoned a protective faerie spirit into the Queen to watch the herds, and that it may be tied to the Mithraic religion; the Legion of Mithras's Alpine meeting place, in sagas that use it, is here.

neighbours.name: Mount Pilatus
neighbours.summary:
A centre of Alpine myth, so crowded with strange inhabitants that some magi think a cluster of regiones opens on its slopes at random: lair of dragons, home of the barbegazi, eyrie of a witch and haunt of a sinner cursed by God. However well it is surveyed, there is always something new on it, in it or terrorising the villages below; it may open into Arcadia, the Magic realm or both. Locals avoid it and punish anyone who climbs it, and magi who settled there would know no peace.

Pontius Pilate's ghost gives it its name. Climbers anger him, and he sends weather that ruins Lucerne's crops and closes the lake; even priests may not climb, for few think they can exorcise a spirit God is justly punishing. His body lies incorrupt in an icy pool, and once a year he comes down to wash his hands in the lake, which turns to blood. Harvesting vis from him is forbidden by the Code. The book gives no aura; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: The Temple of Mercury
neighbours.summary: A ruined Roman temple near Mount Pilatus that Hermetic historians try to tie to the three Founders whose domus magnae border the Alps. The Tribunal met here before the Midsummer Fair drew it to the Icy North. Devices that make illusions still hide it; no magi live there, and it would make an excellent chapter. The book gives no aura; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: The Righi
neighbours.summary: A mountain between Schwyz and Lucerne that peasants call the home of giants. Vast shadows with rainbow edges are cast on its fog: at best, magi know, the ghosts of giants. The death of its last giant set the Tribunal on limiting its own numbers. Journeys End owns it in the Hermetic sense, and hopes giants will settle it again.

neighbours.name: Saint Beatus' Cave
neighbours.summary: Caves in the Jungfrau country lived in by ancient people, said to have been the retreat of a British saint who converted the region and drove out the cave's last tenant, a dragon.

neighbours.name: The Hospice of Saint Bernard
neighbours.summary:
The Benedictine hospice on the Great Saint Bernard pass, founded in 962 by Bernard of Menthon, who led it for forty years and was made a saint; he founded a second house on the Little Saint Bernard. Saracens razed it late in the eleventh century; refounded in 1123, it took his name. Before it stood a temple of the Celtic mountain god, then of Roman Jupiter, and the monks gather the relics of it that surface. Its monks rescue lost travellers, with the great dogs bred from Roman war hounds, and their presence guards the passes from the blizzard demons.

The Code protects it. House Jerbiton helps it name the dead; House Mercere's merchant house funds it at times, and its merchants find it an essential waypoint. Divine 5 (a major monastery, DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: The Saint Gotthard Pass
neighbours.summary: Opened to travellers on foot around 1220, the most direct road from Basel and Zurich to Italy, and being made ready for pack animals; it will drain trade from the other passes. Its Devil's Bridge was built by the Devil, locals say, and they show the boulders he threw when cheated of his price; the abbot of Einsiedeln says he paid for it. Redcaps used the pass long before mundanes did.

neighbours.name: Saint Pierre
neighbours.summary: A tiny village with a column Constantine raised in 339 at the top of the Saint Bernard pass, in place of a statue of Jupiter Penninus he had destroyed.

neighbours.name: The Rosegarten
neighbours.summary: The still-open regio of Laurens, the dwarf king of a land of roses in the Catinaccio of the Val Gardena. He stole a faerie princess, was followed home by her kin along the path of roses, and was taken prisoner; escaping, he cursed the roses to look like stone by day and by night. At dusk, when the sun lies low, they show, wreathing the mountains red. The book gives no aura; Faerie 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: Val Fanes
neighbours.summary: A valley where the Fanes, a kind of faerie, once ruled a mighty kingdom before humans conquered them in ancient times; they hide, awaiting their revenge and the rebuilding of their palaces. Chapels on their places of power have bottled many of them up, leaving other sites unguarded and harvestable, so Valnastium favours priests. Andru's war on one of their kings was pardoned in 1194, and gossip says he took a summer prince's crown. The book gives no aura; Faerie 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: Vorarlberg
neighbours.summary:
A small land on the upper Rhine's flood plain round Bregenz, the old Roman fortress, notable for its isolated villages and high faerie auras; Venedigers, "men from Venice", are a kind of faerie here.

Its dragons belong to storms and avalanches, not fire, and wandering scholars deal with them: a beggar wrecked a farm at Bezau with a dragon on a red rope; Lake Sonderdach's dragon warns swimmers off; a dragon guards a scholar's hoard in a cave of the Vale Galina; a Venetian rode one away from Sontag; and at Brand a scholar's storm buried another under the rubble called the Grave of the Dragon. The book gives no aura; Faerie 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: The Danube
neighbours.summary:
Rising in the Black Forest and fed by the Alps, it flows south-east past Regensburg and Vienna and out of the Tribunal toward the Black Sea, navigable nearly all its length though it floods, runs low and freezes in parts. Goods are still portaged to the Main as the Romans did; Mercere magi like Charlemagne's idea of a canal, but see no way to help it without breaching the Code. Sinews of Knowledge lies behind a cataract that feeds it.

It is Danu's river: the goddess of a web of rivers across Europe, faded with the old powers, whose nymphs keep jewelled regiones in her waters and whose springs open on ways to Arcadia and its great River. She is beyond statistics and no longer deals with mortals.

neighbours.name: Mittenwald
neighbours.summary: Home of a master carver of the finest instruments. When he dies, another of the village's instrument makers becomes the master within a day, inheriting even some of his memories, his debts and unfinished commissions: atavism, one of the oldest forms of magic. His technique itself is quite mundane.

neighbours.name: The Augsburg Tunnels
neighbours.summary: Secret tunnels under Augsburg joining two churches on either side of the city, whose walls mix Hermetic symbols with sacred images: the home, the Quaesitores and Jerbiton and Criamon magi think, of a religious magus whose name and fate are unknown. No covenant claims them; the city's Dominion has put off would-be chapters.

neighbours.name: The Statue of Trivia
neighbours.summary: A small regio west of Eisenstadt, where the Burgenland marks the border with Transylvania, holding a marble statue of Trivia, the threefold goddess of the roads. The Redcaps use it to exchange messages. The book gives no aura; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: Dachstein
neighbours.summary:
Ice caves near Dachstein lead into a regio where a community of giants lives: a dull majority ruled by a small caste of devious magic-weavers who sometimes play simple. They forage in Arcadia, but their gate opens on the Summer lands; they say they are a raiding party driven out by Summer faeries, with an ancestral home on the edge of Arcadian Winter where giants are larger and wiser.

They are allies of Journeys End and trade with it. They value iron, which they use to poison their enemies, and want above all the Banner of Winter, which would let them stay long in the hot Summer lands.

levels.name: The giants' regio
levels.enter: Through the ice caves near Dachstein.
levels.notes: The book gives no aura; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: The Dolomites
neighbours.summary:
Pale limestone mountains in the Tribunal's south-east, worn into stark shapes like single great rocks, that blaze at dawn and dusk and glow white by day. Folk say the Salvani gnomes wove moonlight into them so that a prince's bride from the Moon would not pine.

Most nights a faerie aura rises in their wild places by the Moon: 1, 2 at the full, none when there is no Moon; where a Bright faerie aura is already, it adds to it. Coral is found in the rocks of the highest peaks. Valnastium and Journeys End each suspect the other of keeping the way to the Lunar Faerie realm to itself.

neighbours.name: Klagenfurt
neighbours.summary: A Carinthian town refounded in 1161, where the villagers could not drain the marshes for the lindworm, a dragon fond of virgins, until Herakles passed by and killed it. They keep its skull still.

neighbours.name: The Habach Emerald Mine
neighbours.summary: Europe's only real source of emeralds, worked by the Romans in the Habach valley near Salzburg; no one knows where it is. Some say faeries took the stones, others that an ancient magus hid it and his defences may yet wear away.

neighbours.name: Saint Wolfgang
neighbours.summary: A church in the Abersee valley, where in 976 the priest Wolfgang threw his axe and built where it fell, then beat the Devil so that he could never harm it. It is a pilgrimage site, and the demon-haunted retire here: one of its monks may be a mighty magus hiding from the servants of demons he banished. Divine 4 (a place of worship, DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Schwyz
neighbours.summary: Just before 1200 the monks of Einsiedeln were given the lands round Schwyz as empty waste. The Schwytzers, who disagreed, fell on the abbey's tenants and have since joined the coalitions against the Emperor; Frederick II, now Emperor, is their ally. That a whole people could be overlooked amazes even magi, and many tie their sudden appearance to the Vanishing Away at nearby Tarragon Vale.

neighbours.name: Staubbach Fall
neighbours.summary: The Dust Fall near Lauterbrunnen, so high and thin that its water turns to mist before it lands, like a veil in the wind; in winter a vast upturned icicle rises halfway up it. It is a public vis source of Imaginem in the Code, whose harvesting right is traded among the Tribunal's magi as a costly barter good: Paxon of Verditius holds it now, finds it far from home, and would sell for an intriguing offer. The book gives neither its aura nor its yield; Magic 3 is inferred.

neighbours.name: The Werfen Ice Caves
neighbours.summary:
A maze of ice caves near Werfen, reached only on foot over hard ground, with a magic aura of 4 and a fountain that pours out 30 pawns of Imaginem vis a year. The Code mentions them more than once; no covenant can claim the source, as none can show it can use it steadily. It lies near Salzburg and the trade road from the Brenner, and Werfen village could supply covenfolk.

Two chapters have been tried here. One failed from bad planning; the members of the other were found dead without a wound, some having cut syllables of gibberish into the ice. The common guess is a lucifugus; others think of a delirium-bringing spirit of disease or a monster that sleeps between meals, like an ice wyrm.

neighbours.name: The Wörthsee
neighbours.summary: A Carinthian lake over a drowned town of sinners: a tiny man with a tiny keg, an agent of God's wrath, warned the inn to mend its ways, was mocked, and pulled the bung. Sailors at night still hear the church bells under the water.

neighbours.name: The Rorschach Chapter
neighbours.summary: A tiny chapter house just outside Rorschach, a trading village on Lake Constance near the abbots of Saint Gallen's palace, home of two Mercere magi. The trade through the town covers the House's work in the Tribunal; a Hermes Portal joins it to the motherhouse and so to other chapters, and it offers a fifth of the vis for any new portal it may use. Salt, inks and vellum come cheaply through it. It holds a large property in Vienna in the name of House Mercere's trading house.

neighbours.name: Juno's Spire
neighbours.summary: Archmage Pietro's own chapter. Its Hermes Portal to the motherhouse, a relic of the days of strife within the covenant, sits in a room that can be barred with a thick metal plate and enchanted to burn all human flesh in it on command; that it is widely known feeds the rumour that Pietro is the Antares.

neighbours.name: The Tower of Ashes
neighbours.summary: The home of Archmaga Jacinta of Flambeau.

neighbours.name: Valnastium's Vienna Chapter
neighbours.summary: Valnastium's small chapter in Vienna, joined to the valley by a Hermes Portal. Its magi supply the covenant with goods and live under the city's full Dominion, behind false owners for its houses and shops.

neighbours.name: Valnastium's Constance Chapter
neighbours.summary: Valnastium's small chapter in Constance, joined to the valley by a Hermes Portal. Its magi supply the covenant with goods and live under the city's full Dominion, behind false owners for its houses and shops.

neighbours.name: Valnastium's Saint Gallen Chapter
neighbours.summary: Valnastium's small chapter in Saint Gallen, joined to the valley by a Hermes Portal. Its magi supply the covenant with goods and live under the city's full Dominion, behind false owners for its houses and shops.

neighbours.name: Valnastium's Geneva Chapter
neighbours.summary: Valnastium's small chapter in Geneva, joined to the valley by a Hermes Portal. Its magi supply the covenant with goods and live under the city's full Dominion, behind false owners for its houses and shops.

neighbours.name: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor
neighbours.summary:
King of the Germans, crowned Emperor in Rome late in 1220. Zurich came under him in 1218, and Berne the same year; the Schwytzers are his allies against his rivals.

The book names no ruler; history's for 1220 is given, marked so.

neighbours.name: Leopold VI, Duke of Austria
neighbours.summary:
The Babenberg duke of Austria and Styria, whose house holds the eastern marches. His seat has been Vienna since 1156; his family founded a mint there in 1190. The archbishop of Salzburg opposes him.

The book names no ruler; history's for 1220 is given, marked so.

neighbours.name: Louis I Wittelsbach, Count Palatine of the Rhine
neighbours.summary:
Duke of Bavaria, of the Wittelsbachs who have ruled it since 1180 and won the Rhenish Palatinate in 1214. His seat is Regensburg on the Danube.

The book names no ruler; history's for 1220 is given, marked so.

neighbours.name: Thomas I, Count of Savoy
neighbours.summary:
The House of Savoy holds the Tribunal's lands in the Kingdom of Burgundy and rings the count of Geneva's with forts, and goes on building castles round Fribourg (Gruyères, Estavayer, Morat). Journeys End claims many vis sources in Savoy, and most Alpine covenants keep a chapter there to gather vis; the land has been ill-omened for the Order, its settlements destroyed in the Schism War and the purge of House Tytalus, and some say the next crisis will be heralded by a Hermetic settlement's fall here.

The book names no ruler; history's for 1220 is given, marked so.

neighbours.name: The Counts of Kyburg
neighbours.summary: Their home castle stands outside Winterthur near Zurich, with a vassal's second castle overlooking the town; their lands run north to the Rhine and east to Lake Constance, with about a hundred castles held of them. They inherited the Zähringers' lands in 1217. The book names no count.

neighbours.name: The Hapsburgs
neighbours.summary: A noble house named for the castle Bishop Werner of Strasbourg built in the ruins of Vindonissa; a lesser scion lives there, by his ancestors' graves. A vassal of theirs holds Oberhofen on Lake Thun. The book names no count.

neighbours.name: The House of Zähringen
neighbours.summary: Extinct since Berthold V died in 1217; its lands went to the Kyburgs. The Zähringers founded Fribourg (Berthold IV, 1157), Berne (Berthold V, 1191) and Thun, and set the nobles' craze for building towns and castles.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Basel
neighbours.summary: Has ruled Basel since 1032; its cathedral is less than two centuries old.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Constance
neighbours.summary: Rules the city, perhaps the richest bishopric north of the Alps; a decisive bishop counts in both secular and Church politics. The Code names Constance a place where even minor violence is interference with the Church. A bishop of Constance came to consecrate Einsiedeln's church in 968 and heard God had done it.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Chur
neighbours.summary: A see eight hundred years old; its new cathedral was finished about 1150. Round it Rhaetia lives under club law, scattered with petty castles whose lords squeeze their peasants. The book names no bishop.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Geneva
neighbours.summary: Rules the city, a Roman see; the count of Geneva rules the lands about it.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Lausanne
neighbours.summary: Rebuilding his cathedral slowly, for the castle-building has taken every labourer and mason. The book names no bishop.

neighbours.name: The Bishop of Regensburg
neighbours.summary: His cathedral, begun last century, is still unfinished: each bishop adds to its tangled design, and something indefinable keeps it from completion; the Devil is said to build cathedrals here.

neighbours.name: The Archbishop of Salzburg
neighbours.summary: A powerful archbishop who opposes the duke of Austria, in an impregnable castle never taken by siege. He keeps the Ring of Saint Maurice, a relic said to make its wearer undefeatable in battle; Saint Maurice was a soldier martyred in 302 for refusing to worship the Roman gods.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of Saint Gallen
neighbours.summary:
Grown from the hermitage of Gallus of Iona, who fell into a briar, took it for God's sign, and built his cell with a bear's help. It became a centre of learning that sent out monks to found houses; its library, the Stiftsbibliothek, is marvellous still, though its prestige has waned. In the tenth century an abbot walled the town and with perhaps a hundred armed monks conquered his neighbours; the abbots have ruled many lands round it since, with a palace near Rorschach.

The abbot is Valnastium's ally. The book names none.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of Einsiedeln
neighbours.summary:
Where Saint Meinrad, praying before a figure of the Virgin, was murdered in 861 and his tame ravens followed his killers to Zurich. In 968 an angelic voice told the bishop consecrating its new church that God had consecrated it already; the Pope made the chapel a place of plenary indulgence, and it is the Tribunal's greatest pilgrimage, with a torchlight procession each 14 September.

Second only to Saint Gallen in secular power among the western abbeys, its abbots are great princes served by hereditary noble officers. They say they paid for the Devil's Bridge on the Saint Gotthard; they were given the lands round Schwyz as waste, and its people fell on their tenants. The book names no abbot.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of Reichenau
neighbours.summary: A Benedictine abbey that owns its island and estates down through the Alps to Italy. Charles the Fat, who died here in 888, lies in its Münster church among dozens of spurious treasures: a water pot of Cana, and Charlemagne's 28-pound "emerald", which is glass. Merinita magi think the fakes come of a wager between one of theirs and a local faerie queen, who paid him vis for each ever more flagrant forgery the Church accepted; the right to the wager may have passed to an heir.

neighbours.name: The Abbey of Melk
neighbours.summary: Once a Babenberg castle, given to the Benedictines a century and a half ago. Its monks collect and catalogue knowledge, and its library is excellent. It answers to the Pope with no bishop between, and rumour ties it to a school for magi who take monastic and military vows to war on demons.

neighbours.name: Basel
neighbours.summary:
Founded by the Romans in AD 44, near the highest navigable point of the Rhine, facing a smaller settlement across the river that it also governs: a cosmopolitan city of merchants and usurers. Basilisks hatch here more often than elsewhere.

House Mercere owns the Copper Rooster inn here, named euphemistically for the basilisk: a message point and resting place for Redcaps of three Tribunals, who change horses, restock and leave or collect letters bound across the borders. Old Redcaps retire to it and train apprentices, so some tenants seem to lodge for ever.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Berne
neighbours.summary:
Founded in 1191 by Berthold V of Zähringen, who killed a huge bear the day he laid its first stone and named it for his prize; the Emperor's since 1218, and eyeing its neighbours' villages. The Celts here worshipped a bear goddess, Artio; folk tales tell of an army of bears led by a talking bear, and a merchant's daughter married to a bear. The talking bears' home is unknown to the Order.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Constance
neighbours.summary:
The chief city on Lake Constance, regulating the trade from Bavaria into the Alps; its merchants and its bishop, who rules it, are very rich. Valnastium keeps a chapter here.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Fribourg
neighbours.summary:
South-west of Berne, founded by Berthold IV of Zähringen in 1157, now ringed by Savoy's new castles. Folk say that staying up on Saint John's Eve one may catch the fiery golden seeds of ferns, which the Devil's servants must buy with a bag of money; magi think them Ignem vis, "the blood of the Sun".

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Geneva
neighbours.summary:
A rich city, ruled by the Romans, who made it a see, then by the Burgundians; its bishop rules it, its count the lands round it, and Savoy's forts ring both. Valnastium keeps a chapter here.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Lausanne
neighbours.summary:
A fortified town near Geneva, settled by survivors of the Alemannic attacks on Roman Lousonna, set to hold the approaches to the Saint Bernard.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Lucerne
neighbours.summary:
A small fishing village near Mount Pilatus that grows rich and important as the Saint Gotthard opens. A girl here tells of a barbegazi who gave her healing herbs and a cheese that turned to gold, and of the avalanche that buried her heartless uncle. A dragonet near the town killed its killer with its corrosive blood.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Chur
neighbours.summary:
The chief town of Rhaetia, once a Roman colony.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Zurich
neighbours.summary:
Roman Turicum, a customs port for Gaul's textiles bound south, grown with the trade; under Frederick since 1218.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Interlaken
neighbours.summary:
On a strip of land between the lakes of Thun and Brienz, a docking point for merchants bound south, under Unspunnen castle. The Unspunnens' line ended in the beautiful Ida, whom Rudolph of Wadenschwyl, of a Zähringer house, carried off; years later he brought her and their son home, and the count founded yearly games of racing, stone-throwing and wrestling to mark the day.

The Harder Man, a face in Mount Harder's rocks, is said to be a possessed monk who drove a child off a cliff, set in stone to wait for the Last Day. Thun's castle is a Zähringer one, Oberhofen a Hapsburg vassal's, and Spiez, between Thun and Interlaken, was founded by Attila. The book names no lord here; the Kyburgs inherited the Zähringers.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Augsburg
neighbours.summary:
Very rich from its gold, silver and copper mines, and of great prestige; secret tunnels lie under it.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Munich
neighbours.summary:
A town grown round a Benedictine monastery of the 700s, and still growing.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Regensburg
neighbours.summary:
The duke of Bavaria's seat and the region's richest city, astride the Danube where deep-draughted ships can go no further, trading east and over the Brenner into Italy, so that Italian fashions show in its richer streets. (The book spells it Regensberg.)

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Salzburg
neighbours.summary:
The chief town of a broad Alpine land since the Romans mined its salt; it escaped the barbarians who wasted its neighbours and drew their refugees, and its leaders have long counted in the region. The archbishop's seat.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: Vienna
neighbours.summary:
At the crossing of the Danube and the road from the Baltic to Italy: a Roman city abandoned on a saint's advice, a village for five hundred years, then a crusaders' last German halt; a town by 1137, the duke's seat since 1156, with a mint from 1190 and by 1200 a great stop on the road to Venice, rich in wine.

The Rorschach Chapter holds a large property here in the name of House Mercere's trading house, and Valnastium keeps a chapter. A basilisk hatched in a house here in 1212; the people chased it into a well and stoned it in, and several covenants would thank anyone who learnt its fate.

Divine 3 over most of it (DE p. 418).

neighbours.name: The Rowan Sisterhood
neighbours.summary: An informal society founded in the purge of the Shadow Flambeau and led by Archmaga Jacinta, all but inactive now, whose members still watch for diabolic or vampiric corruption and keep a scattered store of specialised spells and items. Membership passes to a member's eldest filius or filia, so some sisters are men, which is kept quiet: it makes the group seem smaller.

neighbours.name: The Craft School
neighbours.summary: A Hermetic movement that prizes beautiful and useful objects; most Crafters are mage-smiths. Constance of Valnastium leads it, and Angela belongs. Crafters buy odd things at the Fair for their art, and vie with natural magicians for objects of virtue.

neighbours.name: The Jovians
neighbours.summary: Archmage Pietro's lineage within House Flambeau, Auram magi who must learn the Incantation of Lightning and a longer Wings of the Soaring Wind, and master the first; some Flambeau call them interlopers. The book's Pietrine lineage package is a Fourth Edition one and stays in the book.

neighbours.name: The Black Mark
neighbours.summary: A splinter of House Criamon which believes the Dominion will destroy all magic on Earth unless stopped, and denies that it comes from an almighty God.

neighbours.name: The Cult of Dyssynergy
neighbours.summary: House Criamon's bugbear, which may not exist: its members are said to oppose humanity's rush into Twilight, for reasons that change with the teller, and are feared as diabolists are in other Houses. If the Cult of Twilight is in a saga, the Cave is one of its centres and the Dyssynergists want to subvert it.

neighbours.name: The Abbaye des Vignerons
neighbours.summary: A society of vine growers centred on Vevey that acts like a gild, rewarding skilled growers with medals and pruning shears. Every fifteen or twenty years it holds a festival: the best grower is crowned, and the village's loveliest girl gets a dowry and the husband she chooses. Bronze tools were once given to the Rhaetians' goddess, so it may be very old.

neighbours.name: The Ostracism of Athena Alpina
neighbours.summary: Athena Alpina, chief Quaesitor for fourteen years, was trained in the Roman Tribunal and does not share her neighbours' ill will toward House Tremere: she wants a greater part for them in the Tribunal, and her even-handedness looks to Alpine eyes like blatant favouritism. At the meeting of 1214 she had to send away a Tremere hoplite. The sherds at the next meeting may name her.

details.antagonist: The Tribunal's old grudge against House Tremere

stages.title: The meeting of 1221
stages.clues: Magi weigh who will get the most sherds; Athena's dealings with the Tremere are talked of at the Midsummer Fair.
stages.ignored: If one magus in four names her, she must leave the Greater Alps before the second full moon, for twenty-one years; her deputy Cato becomes chief Quaesitor.
stages.stopped: Enough blank sherds, or another name, and she stays.

secrets.title: Why Cato came to the Alps
secrets.text: Cato was sent to the Alps partly so that, if Athena Alpina goes, the chief Quaesitor's place passes to him and not to Adrasteia of Tytalus.

neighbours.name: Raids on the Bavarian Common
neighbours.summary: Magi of the Rhine and Transylvania cross the borders to plunder the vis sources the Code calls Alpine, the Bavarian Common above all, which the Quaesitores harvest and divide at the Fair. Adrasteia of Tytalus and Katrina of Bjornaer hunt the raiders, baiting traps for the greedy and striking only those caught in the act; counter-raiders are fair game to them too.

details.antagonist: Vis poachers of the Rhine and Transylvania

stages.title: A trap is sprung
stages.clues: A vis site of the Common is found stripped; a stranger is seen near another.
stages.ignored: The poachers grow bolder, and Alpine magi talk of counter-raids into the Rhineland.
stages.stopped: Adrasteia's ambush takes them in the act.

neighbours.name: The Sicilian Children
neighbours.summary: Five years ago a magical accident in Sicily brought about the birth of two dozen Gifted children at once. The Icy North motherhouse offers a chair to whoever makes the best use of its empty buildings, and many expect a school for the children: the likeliest proposal trains them collegially, an untried method, and the Quaesitores favour it, since two dozen magi of one age and one affinity graduating into a single House might unbalance the Order.

details.antagonist: The rival claimants to the empty buildings

stages.title: The chair is awarded
stages.clues: Claimants put their proposals to the motherhouse; Houses that want the children for themselves stir.
stages.ignored: The collegial school is founded, and the children come to the Alps.
stages.turned: A troupe that wins the chair founds the school itself.

neighbours.name: The Vanishing Away
neighbours.summary:
Twenty-two years ago the four magi of Tarragon Vale and their covenfolk vanished. The Quaesitores hold their vis and will settle no estate without proof of death; the heirs want the hoard. Many tie the vanishing to the sudden appearance of the Schwytzers nearby.

If the troupe solves it, they hold knowledge worth a great deal to rich heirs, and might ask to settle Tarragon Vale, taking on its legal standing, its debts and its unknown supernatural enemies, and the things in its sealed basements. If someone else solves it, the vis and the sources are shared out, and some heirs move to the Alps while others sell.

neighbours.name: Jacinta and the Flambeau Primacy
neighbours.summary: Archmaga Jacinta is the eldest of her line and the most able Perdo maga in the Order. If the few Flambeau older or deadlier than she die first, she may be declared Prima, making the Icy North her House's temporary domus magna, to her neighbours' resigned disgust; others hope a younger, more distant fire magus is chosen instead.

neighbours.name: The Amaranth Trade
neighbours.summary: The Code orders all amaranth destroyed, but the trade in the faerie flower goes on, around Ingolstadt above all. Taken as a dust in white wine it makes the Gifted see the world's hidden forces and keeps them from looking old, but it addicts them and makes Twilight likelier and worse, and Hermetic magic can neither detect it nor cure the craving. The Quaesitores believe faerie nobles grow it to make magi addicts and command them against the Order; others doubt it.

neighbours.name: Esther in Stone
neighbours.summary: Esther of Criamon was turned to stone by faeries two years ago; her ghost goes about the Cave, and the curse can be undone. The past Primi delay her unpetrifying to study the juno she has become, and her sodales think her death and return, rightly understood, could set her on her path to the Enigma.

neighbours.name: The Banner of Winter
neighbours.summary: The giants of Dachstein want the Banner of Winter above all things: it would let them stay long in the hot Summer lands of Arcadia. Journeys End's magi search for it now and then, unsure they want to give it to their huge allies, who might use it to go deep into Arcadia or to rampage across Mythic Europe.

neighbours.name: The Vienna Basilisk
neighbours.summary: A basilisk hatched in a house in Vienna in 1212. The townsfolk chased it into a well and poured stones on it; magi doubt that killed it, and even if it did, it lies dead in the groundwater. Several covenants would thank anyone who learnt its fate. Kentigern suspects a magus is making basilisks.

neighbours.name: The Deaths at Werfen
neighbours.summary: Thirty pawns of Imaginem a year pour from a fountain in Werfen's ice caves, unclaimed. The second chapter to try for them was found dead without a wound, gibberish cut into the ice. A lucifugus is the common guess; a spirit of delirium or a sleeping ice wyrm are others.

neighbours.name: Sinews of Knowledge's Money
neighbours.summary: Sinews of Knowledge has been caught again and again making goods from vis to sell, and has no income now; it cannot dispose of what it makes discreetly. It weighs a Hermes Portal to a chapter in another Tribunal, preferably eastward, or an alliance with a young covenant on the frontier, which would give that covenant the Alps' trade and make it depend on Sinews. Young magi who solve its money troubles would surely be offered a place.

details.antagonist: The Tribunal's ban on flagrant spending

links.note: Its liaison to a trading partner

characters.name: Muscaria

description.biography: Sanctuary of Ice: The Greater Alps Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Prima of House Criamon, filia Demetrius, forty-one and looking an energetic adolescent who knows far too much: her master, an alchemist, gave her a longevity potion at fourteen, and she has kept her body from growing up in his honour. Named for the mushroom the first local magicians used, she finds such compounds dull, doubts her own insights, and chose to support others instead, building the mushroom farms that feed the living. She did not expect the Primacy: it is the wish to give up wisdom to serve others, not wisdom, that marks a Primus. She leads the council of magi and elected covenfolk, and dislikes obfuscation (DE p. 21; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp. 44, 56).

characters.name: Circum Perfico

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 120 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filia Johannes, an elderly maga who believes a Hermes Portal between the Cave and the North Pole would line up the Earth's axis with its magical and magnetic fields, making the Earth more like the stars, so that the answer to the Enigma could exist in it without being sullied.

characters.name: Darius

The book gives no age: 90 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filius Yannes, a Muto Mentem specialist with strong Intellego and Herbam who brews mind-altering substances, alcohol above all. Popular with grogs across Europe and drunk much of the time, he studies drunken mobs, spikes the wells of remote villages, and is to host the nine-yearly meeting of magical brewers in 1226. The Quaesitores blame him for much of the petty trouble at the Midsummer Fair. He holds that the Enigma's answer will take the mundanes into the Twilight lineage, and that ecstasy is the one philosophy they will accept.

characters.name: Echo

characters.summary: Filia Gribbinus, a pleasant, bland maga in her sixties, a Mentem specialist with an affinity for ghosts, who is gaining little wisdom for an illicit affair. If it came out, her covenmates would send her from the Central Clutch for her own good. She and Esther, trained by the same master, argue often.

characters.name: Esther

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 60 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filia Gribbinus, once an Imaginem specialist, turned to stone by faeries a couple of years ago. Her ghost floated free when the statue came home, but the curse can be undone, so she may not be dead; she is unsure whether she is a projected image, a ghost, or a spirit that thinks it is Esther, and fears she is someone else's figment. Arguably a member of the covenant: no one is sure.

characters.name: Fortuito

description.biography: Sanctuary of Ice: The Greater Alps Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 50 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filius Circum Perfico, who travels Europe studying diviners and seers to learn where their knowledge comes from. He sends letters dated before a disaster, to be delivered only after it, asking how its survivors lived, since a warning would spoil his observations, and many magi never forgive him. A Seeker of sorts, he is browbeaten by others for what he withholds.

characters.name: Gunther

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. characters.summary: Filius Frederico, the covenant's chief baker, who no longer studies magic and acts as little like a magus as he can, seeking wisdom in the small perfect moments of mundane life.

characters.name: Hagen

characters.summary: Filius Flauberto the Difficult, who makes atonal music with summoned spirits, believing a hidden composition resonates under the world's events. Many of his line were driven mad by Plato's Comma, the flaw in the seven notes that answer the seven planets.

characters.name: Latrunculus

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 55 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filius Aurelia, a skilled Terram magus and surveyor who believes the Roman roads overlie magical paths, with the Great Ones buried at the great crossings under the cities; reckon finely enough and one could dig up an ancient. Seekers consult him, and he may go to Egypt to help catalogue a cat cemetery, with younger, more violent magi.

characters.name: Pellam

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 30 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filius Cato, a young magus who believes ball games are the folk remnants of pagan rites that might lead toward the Enigma or the Seekers' sacred places; Darius's ally.

characters.name: Phalene

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 50 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filia Innocu, who sees Twilight as a metamorphosis like a moth's and studies creatures that transform. Her philosophy has people outgrowing the Enigma, the House's politics wrong and the Primi's sacrifice pointless, so she does not debate it.

characters.name: Regina

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. characters.summary: Filia Gribbinus, first trained in House Bonisagus by Dexter, whose long study of the Enigma has drawn her into Criamon. She makes mystical spaces in which things impossible in the mundane world become possible.

characters.name: Siobhan

The book gives no age: 55 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filia Vespasian the Avaricious, from Hibernia, with plain links to Bright Summer: the House's specialist in faeries, a Vim maga with weaker Arts than most of her House, who retrained under a Merinita to learn Faerie Magic. She holds Twilight and deep Arcadia to be the same place. Her three apprentices share her air of knowing more than one could understand.

characters.name: Viscus

description.biography: Sanctuary of Ice: The Greater Alps Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 60 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Filius Circum Perfico, a haruspex who seeks the Enigma in the entrails of magical beasts, and of familiars most of all; he once looked at the liver of a young Jerbiton killed in a lab accident. Magi send him the remains of beasts whose vis they have cut out, which makes him the Redcaps' least favourite magus, and his bottled oddities sell at the Fair.

characters.name: Athena Alpina

description.biography: Sanctuary of Ice: The Greater Alps Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The chief Quaesitor of the Alps for fourteen years, appointed by the Primus of Guernicus; called Alpina to tell her from the many Athenas of her House. An Intellego specialist most interested in Hermetic contracts of trade and sale, she runs the Fair and arranges the exchange of listed sites between covenants. Respected for her post and disliked as a person, since she lacks her neighbours' biases: trained in the Roman Tribunal, she does not dislike the Tremere and wants them to play a larger part. She is a hundred and twelve and looks in her late sixties, of Slavic blood, dark-haired, tall and solid, and travels in the stola with its veil, lifting it to speak in public.

characters.summary: The second most senior quaesitor in the Tribunal and Athena's deputy, who spies in disguise as a crumpled drunk old man (or a busty serving maid), letting magi take him for a magical incompetent until his subtle illusions catch them.

characters.name: Adrasteia

The book gives no age: 60 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A quaesitor of House Tytalus, chosen for stealth and defensive violence, who roams the borders hunting raiders who plunder the vis sites the Code calls Alpine. Allowed to strike only those caught in the act, she lays elaborate traps and ruses, always with two hoplites at her back. Elsewhere her methods would not pass; here the powerful covenants wish for more like her, and the Primus of Guernicus, who sees she may become a problem, keeps her because she deters vigilantes and counter-raids, which she treats as fair game too.

characters.name: Kentigern

invented_spells.name: Call the Basilisk
invented_spells.description: Creates a basilisk, which Kentigern made to study them safely: they are oddly common near Basel and Vienna, where an egg laid in a dung heap is said to be enough, and he suspects a magus makes them. Spell focus a toad, or being where basilisks are common (+1). DE: create a magical beast, Base 50 (with Vim for its magical nature), +1 Touch, +2 Sun = 65; the book's level 50.

invented_spells.name: The Foes of the Ibis
invented_spells.description: Creates a small flock of iaculi, winged snakes; one of Kentigern's favourite combat spells, often made invisible. Magi think iaculi ill-omened and able to slip Hermetic protections, which is untrue and which he does not correct. Spell focus a dead ibis (+5). DE: Base 50, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 Group = 75; the book's level 40.

invented_spells.name: Daughter of Zephyrs
invented_spells.description: Creates a magical horse that gallops through the air as others do on land; Kentigern has used vis to keep one for good. Spell focus silver horseshoes (+3). DE: Base 50, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 size = 70; the book's level 45.

invented_spells.name: Vision of the Marauding Beast
invented_spells.description: A Fourth Edition spell the book lists without a description and the catalog lacks, with no catalog spell of its Arts and level to stand in for it; its printed level is kept.

invented_spells.name: To Know the Owner as Might His Hound
invented_spells.description: Senses what an animal senses, cast on domestic beasts or on one of his flying serpents. DE: read an animal's surface thoughts, Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun = 25, as printed.

invented_spells.name: Liar's Chime
invented_spells.description: Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie with an Imaginem requisite: a bell rings when the target lies, since all breath looks frosty in the Alps. DE: Base 10, +1 Eye, +2 Sun = 25, as printed.

invented_spells.name: The Thief of Memory
invented_spells.description: Removes all memory of one person, place or event; the target often knows something is missing. Made to suppress the Gift of untrained children or take away their memories of home; the Quaesitores use it to tidy up after Hermetic criminals. Spell focus a burning forget-me-not (+3). DE: remove a major or long memory, Base 15, +1 Eye = 20; the book's level 25.

description.biography:
A quaesitor, an office of House Guernicus he holds though he is of Ex Miscellanea. Equipment: a bought longevity charm (-14), a light crossbow, a longsword, and padded leather riding clothes, weightless, warm in the sky and as quilted armour (Protection 2); the covenant's quaesitorial blindfold, which helps detect deceit and reason clearly, borrowed until his own spells are better; he is weighing a self-loading crossbow as his talisman. He knows a greater Soothe the Pains of the Beast that heals six wound levels (DE: heal all wounds, Base 35, +1 Touch = CrAn 40, Ritual).
His familiar is Tobias, a faerie hound who leads his pack, can command other animals, can cast Soothe the Pains of the Beast with his tongue, carries Animal vis on his collar, and through the bond gave Kentigern flight by running and immunity to wind chill. The book prints no stats for him (it points to the Fourth Edition's Faeries), so he has no familiar record here.
His Deficiencies leave only Auram biting: the book's Auram totals, such as True Sight of the Air's +34, use the whole score, and Deficient Form halves them.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 99 as printed (looks 58); Twilight Points 9 / 3 = Warping 3; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 6. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
