characters.summary: A quaesitor of a Hibernian beast-mage tradition with a magical affinity for dogs, whose faerie hounds prowl the Midsummer Fair growling at anyone who smells suspicious. A skilled tracker, he hunts magical beasts through blizzards and air elementals through the sky, and calls on the nearest covenant for a quarry too strong for him. Once a monastic novice, he keeps an interest in the Church and canon law, vets the contracts between mundanes and the covenants' shell houses, and is the quaesitor likeliest to witness an oath. He came three years ago from retraining at Magvillus: a respectable quaesitor and a poor hedge wizard both, and so an unknown quantity.

Arms and reason share a Greek root, and he means to make the world's pieces fit by shoving them. One of the finest exponents of certamen in the Tribunal, with some success against demons; his deadliest spell is a high-level form of the Gift of the Enigma. He will not be called back to the Central Clutch soon.

Hunting a leopard for his hoplite's sash, he was stalked and ambushed by it, and courted it as his familiar: Cinnamon, who catches birds from behind clouds. Many Alpine magi hope she dies before the few Flambeau older or deadlier than she, for as Prima she would make the Icy North her House's domus magna. She leads the Rowan Sisterhood. She and Pietro were born in the same Portuguese village, declared Wizard's War on each other on the same day twenty-eight years ago, and have been allies, rivals, enemies and perhaps lovers since; neither has fought a witnessed certamen. Recruited as a faerie midwife for the covenfolk's hard births, she travels the Order to deliver children too strange for Corpus spells. Her magic is poor for her age, and she cannot take an apprentice. She believes she is the new Amalthea, destined to find and raise the new Jupiter Pennius; her House thinks her mad and has asked the other Bjornaer to keep her from harm.

His mandolin, won in Arcadia, works like Aura of Rightful Authority and lets him speak with living things, but only through a song's lyrics; a flute like it, which commands the elements, is said to be hidden somewhere. characters.summary: Archmaga, filia Rafe, the Longevity Project's chief researcher, slowed because her predecessors all but exhausted its line of work; if she succeeds, magi of middling Corpus could keep themselves until Twilight. Her own contribution is the potion that slows apparent aging. She asks magi to send her the bodies of human-shaped faeries through the Redcaps, freely shares a spell that keeps such bodies from decay, and pays for rare ones; some Merinita hate her for dissecting their kin. A Progressive, who sees Bonisagus as human and fallible and her own generation as no lesser. Many suspect she can strip a man's organs out onto a table; in truth she is no combat maga.

secrets.text: She is an amaranth halfling, daughter of one of the faeries who grow the forbidden flower: immune to it, since her body makes it, she stopped aging at 21 and began gaining Twilight as if under a longevity potion, and expects to fade into Arcadia to join her father.

She makes longevity enchantments for young magi, as tattoos, and is the covenant's chosen liaison to the spring covenant it hopes to trade through. Her sigil, the colour of bone, marks all her work: since her longevity potion she is all bone and ivory, and her fingernails are serrated like an infant's teeth and change with her mood. She keeps company to stay human, knowing that solitude leads to the Tower of Skulls. Her apprentice Augustina, eight years in training, is a bone maga of Animal who wants adventure.

Her devices: a warm copper triangle pin (CrIg 6, constant) that also gives her Eyes of the Cat once a day (MuCo(An) 10); a golden lickstone, a small plate that clings to the palate and hides itself, holding the Seven-League Stride 24 times a day (ReCo 35), which the Rorschach magi let her trade for the Leap of Homecoming she has no use for, living at home; and a copper leaf in each boot, each a pawn of Rego vis, which lets her reroll any die that would give blisters or a turned ankle. She has not had them totalled against the Redcap Virtue's 50 levels and two a year since. Boots of an Alpine dragonette's skin, which she killed herself. A longevity potion, -5.

characters.summary: A Redcap without the Gift, small and level-headed, who looks in her late twenties: a mythic Redcap of the Alps, sure of every safe road between the covenants. She killed an Alpine dragonette herself and wears boots of its skin, of which she is very proud.

description.biography:
He learnt most of his spells from books Valnastium's library trades for, and avoids inventing his own. He knows Eyes of the Cat in a form the book changes to Near, Sun or Year and Group. He does not brew his own longevity potion (-14). He borrows the House's devices, which come to it when a magus dies with no sodalis of his master's master: masks of Disguise of the New Visage or Image Phantom for his agents, and the Standard of the Shadowy Men, carried against the Fanes, with group Seven-League Stride, invisibility and grog-strengthening enchantments. He will not use Enslave the Mortal Mind or its like. His relic is a flake of Saint Cyprian's fingerbone sewn into white silk, to which he wrongly credits his luck. His talisman is a flame-red wedding veil (HoH:S p. 52; Sanctuary of Ice makes it Carmine's sigil, kept by him, as his gold and amethyst ring is kept by her). He and Carmine married by the Greek rite with pagan Hermetic symbols, which they keep quiet.
Converted from the Fourth Edition block by the Definitive Edition's appendix: age 81 as printed (looks 35); Twilight Points 5 / 3 = Warping 1; Confidence 1 (3 points), the Definitive Edition's baseline, not the old 7. Characteristics and Arts as printed; no rebalancing.
Virtues and Flaws: Visual Eidetic Memory dropped (not in the catalog); Great Intelligence as Great Intelligence; Magic Affinity as Minor Magical Focus; True Love (Major): Carmine; Relic: the fingerbone of Saint Cyprian; Susceptible to Divine Power as Susceptibility to Divine Power; Driving Goal as Driven (Minor): to reconcile the Church and the Order; Dutybound: religious; Enemy as Enemies: Yselt of Journeys End.
Abilities: Brawling 1 to Brawl; Certamen 5 to Penetration; Climb 1 to Athletics; Disputatio 3 to Teaching; Forgery 1 to Guile; Greater Alpine Tribunal Lore 4 to Area Lore: Greater Alps Tribunal; Hermetic Law 3 to Code of Hermes; House Jerbiton Lore 8 to Organization Lore: House Jerbiton; Lectio 4 to Teaching; Legend Lore 5 to Area Lore: Greater Alps Tribunal; Magic Affinity 5 to Mentem, 15 xp; Occult Lore 2 to Infernal Lore; Order of Hermes Lore 4 to Organization Lore: Order of Hermes; Play Lute 1 to Music; Scribe Latin 7 to Artes Liberales; Sing 1 to Music; Storyteller 1 to Living Language: Greek; Theology 3 to Theology: Christian.
Spells: Chirurgeon's Healing Touch as The Chirurgeon's Healing Touch; Aura of Ennobled Presence as Aura of the Ennobled Presence; Circular Ward Against Faeries as Circular Ward Against Faerie Spirits; At the catalog's level or Art: Eyes of the Cat MuCo 15 to MuCo 5; Thaumaturgical Transformation of Plants to Iron MuHe(Te) 15 to MuHe 20; Image Phantom MuIm 25 to MuIm 20; The Captive Voice ReIm 15 to ReIm 30; Haunt of the Living Ghost ReIm 35 to CrIm 35; Gift of Reason CrMe 25 to CrMe 35; Circular Ward Against Demons ReVi 35 to ReVi general; Circular Ward Against Faeries ReVi 35 to ReVi general; Opening the Intangible Tunnel ReVi 35 to ReVi general; Watching Ward ReVi 30 to ReVi general.

characters.summary: Primus of House Jerbiton, filius Astrolabe, from Greece: elected Secundus at thirty-eight and Primus at forty-three, in 1182, helped by his fame for finding Akrotiri, the city buried in ash on Thera, whose works of art he recovered until vampires drove him off. Tall, muscular and clean-shaven, with short dark curls, dignified before crowds and warm alone; his hardest spells are illusions. A conciliator who looks conservative but may radicalise his House: he favours open dealings with great mundanes, keeps a network of agents and a vast correspondence, rallied the House to save Constantinople's art, and hopes to show the Church that the Gift is a charism. His talisman is a flame-red wedding veil, and his familiar a small aristocratic cat, Crucifixo (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 52).

characters.summary: Filia Frederich et Vortimer, over a hundred and thirty: trained in House Verditius, she worked for the Jerbiton under contract for fifty years before joining the House. Andru made her his Lesser Secundus, an office the Fifth Edition's House no longer has. A leader of the Craft School, which prizes the beautiful and the useful, she builds soaring, twisting laboratories and simple items for specialist labs; her lab texts sell at the Fair. Her adoptive parens Vortimer is of the lineage of Carolinus. The eldest living magus whose age the book gives, and so the Praeco here.

characters.summary: Filia Susannah of House Flambeau, of mixed Iberian blood, one of the most beautiful women alive, dark-haired and dressed in black. She came in Andru's entourage forty-three years ago, became his model, his mistress and his wife, and is the valley's hostess. She follows the School of Sebastian, works magic on molten metal, and helps House Jerbiton when extreme violence is called for; she has passed the Jerbiton Gauntlet but prefers her independence. A muse. Their children are middle-aged, with grandchildren in their twenties; none has the Gift, and some are autocrats, scribes, priests and librarians (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 52).

characters.name: Josephine
characters.summary: A chef from the Engadine whose food is as good as magic, at home with both noble and peasant cooking: an urban kind of folk magician. characters.name: François
characters.summary: The elderly but powerful blacksmith of the Village of the Vale, whose smithy is one of the most magical places in the valley. His large family serves as grogs; some have a frightening knack with weapons and become sergeants elsewhere, and his journeymen find places in covenants across the Order. A Larta in Sanctuary of Ice, a companion here.

characters.name: Chloe
characters.summary: The valley's chief minstrel, who composes rather than performs: soaring choral prayers, magical when others sing them, often clergy in churches, and a key part of Andru's charm offensive. She seems an odd, perhaps unique, natural magician. A Larta in Sanctuary of Ice, a companion here.

powers.name: Mementos
powers.description: Handles the things she loved in life as if alive. Her gloves make it needless, but most strong ghosts have it.

powers.name: Unquiet Spirit
powers.description: Flings things with her thoughts: in the Cave, up to 250 pounds as far as 100 paces, lighter things falling straight down at the edge of its reach; landing one precisely is a targeting roll, +2 to hit a man-sized target with a small object. ReTe with Animal, Aquam, Corpus or Herbam requisites for what she throws. Fourth Edition: 1 points.

creatures.equipment: Pale grey leather gloves that let her handle things; an elaborate galena chatelaine whose keys, material, magical, spectral and illusory, open every lock in the covenant and more.
creatures.appearance: Tall and lean, dark-haired and speckled with grey, with very dark eyes; her magic is so strong that, when she wishes, she seems entirely solid. She may look any age from her life.
creatures.notes:
The Cave's autocrat, appointed by Criamon himself, who bound her to the place of her death, poisoned, to care for his children until the Enigma is solved; she is no genius loci. She cares chiefly for the Enigma's completion, which is easy to forget, as it so often means seeing to everyone's comfort; those who know it bargain with her better. She can be hurt only by Mentem or Vim magic, and will never possess anyone, which breaks her faith.

Converted: the block's Destiny (to serve the final Criamon magus) has no Definitive Edition Virtue and is kept here; Craft (many) 3 is left out; Forgery 6 is Guile, the better of the two; Confidence 9 is the Definitive Edition's baseline. The text gives her Might as 45 adjusted by the aura; the block's 65 stands (A19).

As printed in Fourth Edition: Fist, in her magical gloves Init +1, Attack -1, Defense +1, Damage +0.

creatures.name: Jane, the Fifth Primus

reputations.name: Will mark the coming of the New Criamon (some Criamon magi)

powers.name: Poltergeist
powers.description: Moves things of extraordinary weight anywhere in the aura, a Might point a magnitude of Target; she seems to touch what she moves. Nothing in the aura less than a year can be moved, though she can push it with other things. Fourth Edition: 3 points.

powers.name: The Primi's Magic
powers.description: Casts any spontaneous spell up to level 25 and any formulaic spell she knows up to level 60, at 1 Might point a magnitude; she earns no Twilight. Points spent come back to the Primi when a new Primus joins them. She knows every Vim and Mentem spell of the core rules to level 60 and many spells to level 25 of other Forms.

creatures.notes:
The youngest of the past Primi who knew Criamon in life, looking about thirty: friendly and approachable, she often offers to tutor outsiders who come to the Cave. Some Criamon believe the Primi will vanish in order shortly before a new Criamon takes the Founder's place, and that Jane will be the last to go. Her block stands for every spectral Primus: their 75 Might is one pool, so points one spends are gone from all.

Sanctuary of Ice makes the slain Primi genii loci bound to the Axis Magica, harmed only by Vim magic and never truly in solid form; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults calls them ghosts of past Primi who serve in place of a library and will one day enter the Hypostasis. The block is recorded as printed, with Confidence at the Definitive Edition's baseline. She never possesses anyone: the Primi think taking on matter like swimming through sewage.

powers.name: Bury in Snow
powers.description: A snowstorm that buries the gnomes and their enemies: the book's Control Auram 8, fixed as a Greater Power, as their Might follows their role.

powers.name: Shake the Mountain
powers.description: Brings snow and rock down on those below: the book's Control Terram 8, fixed as a Greater Power.

powers.name: Faerie Gifts
powers.description: Enchants small objects, as the Fourth Edition's Faeries describes: the cheese one gave a poor girl of Lucerne turned to gold.

creatures.appearance: Small blue gnomes, always male, with icicles in their beards and huge feet they use as skis or to dig through snow.
creatures.notes:
They keep above the tree line and sleep through the summer, and live through much of western Europe in tunnels on peaks that are always snow-capped; their name probably means icicle beards. They shun melee, fighting with the weather. Mundane cold and metal weapons cannot hurt them; the block's Soak +10 is Stamina plus 10. Carlo of Journeys End has their features.

The Lucerne girl's tale: sent to beg from her uncle for her sick mother, she was refused even the rind of his cheese, and met a barbegazi who gave her healing herbs and a cheese that became gold; that night an avalanche buried the uncle and filled his fields with stones.

Might 20 as printed.

As printed in Fourth Edition: Soak +15.

Stamina and Soak as the dwarf, RoP:F p. 96.

creatures.name: Crucifixo
creatures.appearance: A small aristocratic black cat (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 52; Sanctuary of Ice spells him Crucifixio).
creatures.notes:
Andru's familiar, of the Black Lineage: so many Valnastium magi have kept black cats as familiars that a magical strain of them lives in the valley. He could talk before he was bound, and is not the lineage's most senior cat, though his tie to the Primus will speed his rise. His Scribe Latin 5 (he reads, but cannot write) is Artes Liberales and Latin here. The book's Size 0 is kept.

Rebuilt by the Definitive Edition's familiar rules (DE pp. 266-267) from Andru's Lab Total, not copied from the Fourth Edition bond. The book's cords were Gold +2, Silver +2, Bronze 0; the Lab Total buys +2 for the bronze cord too. Its bond qualities are invested powers: Mental Communication (CrMe, DE's own example), an invisibility like the Veil of Invisibility (PeIm 20, +10 for unlimited use), and making people love cats and wish to serve them as princes (CrMe, as Panic of the Trembling Heart, 15, +10 for unlimited use). He could talk before the binding, so the book's Attunement of Speech is not needed.

As printed in Fourth Edition: Claws and teeth Init +5, Attack +5, Defense +7, Damage -3; Soak +0.

calendar.title: The Liberalia
calendar.note: The March feast, the Festival of Welcome of Houses of Hermes: Societates, at which the year's new magi are welcomed and Jerbiton petitions are heard. Valnastium sponsors it, mostly at Tarragon Vale; it is forgone in a Tribunal's year.

calendar.title: The Midsummer Fair
calendar.note: The 3rd to the 10th of June at the Icy North motherhouse: the Quaesitores divide the Bavarian Common, covenants bid in Vim vis at inverse auctions, magi trade and socialise, and informal and Quaesitorial tribunals sit.

muscaria.name: Muscaria
muscaria.summary: Prima of House Criamon, filia Demetrius, forty-one and looking an energetic adolescent who knows far too much: her master, an alchemist, gave her a longevity potion at fourteen, and she has kept her body from growing up in his honour. Named for the mushroom the first local magicians used, she finds such compounds dull, doubts her own insights, and chose to support others instead, building the mushroom farms that feed the living. She did not expect the Primacy: it is the wish to give up wisdom to serve others, not wisdom, that marks a Primus. She leads the council of magi and elected covenfolk, and dislikes obfuscation (DE p. 21; Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp. 44, 56).

circum_perfico.name: Circum Perfico
circum_perfico.summary: Filia Johannes, an elderly maga who believes a Hermes Portal between the Cave and the North Pole would line up the Earth's axis with its magical and magnetic fields, making the Earth more like the stars, so that the answer to the Enigma could exist in it without being sullied.

darius.name: Darius
darius.summary: Filius Yannes, a Muto Mentem specialist with strong Intellego and Herbam who brews mind-altering substances, alcohol above all. Popular with grogs across Europe and drunk much of the time, he studies drunken mobs, spikes the wells of remote villages, and is to host the nine-yearly meeting of magical brewers in 1226. The Quaesitores blame him for much of the petty trouble at the Midsummer Fair. He holds that the Enigma's answer will take the mundanes into the Twilight lineage, and that ecstasy is the one philosophy they will accept.

echo.name: Echo
echo.summary: Filia Gribbinus, a pleasant, bland maga in her sixties, a Mentem specialist with an affinity for ghosts, who is gaining little wisdom for an illicit affair. If it came out, her covenmates would send her from the Central Clutch for her own good. She and Esther, trained by the same master, argue often.

esther.name: Esther
esther.summary: Filia Gribbinus, once an Imaginem specialist, turned to stone by faeries a couple of years ago. Her ghost floated free when the statue came home, but the curse can be undone, so she may not be dead; she is unsure whether she is a projected image, a ghost, or a spirit that thinks it is Esther, and fears she is someone else's figment. Arguably a member of the covenant: no one is sure.

fortuito.name: Fortuito
fortuito.summary: Filius Circum Perfico, who travels Europe studying diviners and seers to learn where their knowledge comes from. He sends letters dated before a disaster, to be delivered only after it, asking how its survivors lived, since a warning would spoil his observations, and many magi never forgive him. A Seeker of sorts, he is browbeaten by others for what he withholds.

gunther.name: Gunther
gunther.summary: Filius Frederico, the covenant's chief baker, who no longer studies magic and acts as little like a magus as he can, seeking wisdom in the small perfect moments of mundane life.

hagen.name: Hagen
hagen.summary: Filius Flauberto the Difficult, who makes atonal music with summoned spirits, believing a hidden composition resonates under the world's events. Many of his line were driven mad by Plato's Comma, the flaw in the seven notes that answer the seven planets.

latrunculus.name: Latrunculus
latrunculus.summary: Filius Aurelia, a skilled Terram magus and surveyor who believes the Roman roads overlie magical paths, with the Great Ones buried at the great crossings under the cities; reckon finely enough and one could dig up an ancient. Seekers consult him, and he may go to Egypt to help catalogue a cat cemetery, with younger, more violent magi.

pellam.name: Pellam
pellam.summary: Filius Cato, a young magus who believes ball games are the folk remnants of pagan rites that might lead toward the Enigma or the Seekers' sacred places; Darius's ally.

phalene.name: Phalene
phalene.summary: Filia Innocu, who sees Twilight as a metamorphosis like a moth's and studies creatures that transform. Her philosophy has people outgrowing the Enigma, the House's politics wrong and the Primi's sacrifice pointless, so she does not debate it.

regina.name: Regina
regina.summary: Filia Gribbinus, first trained in House Bonisagus by Dexter, whose long study of the Enigma has drawn her into Criamon. She makes mystical spaces in which things impossible in the mundane world become possible.

siobhan.name: Siobhan
siobhan.summary: Filia Vespasian the Avaricious, from Hibernia, with plain links to Bright Summer: the House's specialist in faeries, a Vim maga with weaker Arts than most of her House, who retrained under a Merinita to learn Faerie Magic. She holds Twilight and deep Arcadia to be the same place. Her three apprentices share her air of knowing more than one could understand.

viscus.name: Viscus
viscus.summary: Filius Circum Perfico, a haruspex who seeks the Enigma in the entrails of magical beasts, and of familiars most of all; he once looked at the liver of a young Jerbiton killed in a lab accident. Magi send him the remains of beasts whose vis they have cut out, which makes him the Redcaps' least favourite magus, and his bottled oddities sell at the Fair.

athena_alpina.name: Athena Alpina
athena_alpina.summary: The chief Quaesitor of the Alps for fourteen years, appointed by the Primus of Guernicus; called Alpina to tell her from the many Athenas of her House. An Intellego specialist most interested in Hermetic contracts of trade and sale, she runs the Fair and arranges the exchange of listed sites between covenants. Respected for her post and disliked as a person, since she lacks her neighbours' biases: trained in the Roman Tribunal, she does not dislike the Tremere and wants them to play a larger part. She is a hundred and twelve and looks in her late sixties, of Slavic blood, dark-haired, tall and solid, and travels in the stola with its veil, lifting it to speak in public.

cato.name: Cato
cato.summary: The second most senior quaesitor in the Tribunal and Athena's deputy, who spies in disguise as a crumpled drunk old man (or a busty serving maid), letting magi take him for a magical incompetent until his subtle illusions catch them.

adrasteia.name: Adrasteia
adrasteia.summary: A quaesitor of House Tytalus, chosen for stealth and defensive violence, who roams the borders hunting raiders who plunder the vis sites the Code calls Alpine. Allowed to strike only those caught in the act, she lays elaborate traps and ruses, always with two hoplites at her back. Elsewhere her methods would not pass; here the powerful covenants wish for more like her, and the Primus of Guernicus, who sees she may become a problem, keeps her because she deters vigilantes and counter-raids, which she treats as fair game too.

vincent.name: Vincent
vincent.summary: An archmage of Criamon and a hoplite, who seeks the Enigma through the violent application of magic to the body: his spells, he holds, purify his enemies and teach them not to break the Code. Arms and reason share a Greek root, and he means to make the world's pieces fit by shoving them. One of the finest exponents of certamen in the Tribunal, with some success against demons; his deadliest spell is a high-level form of the Gift of the Enigma. He will not be called back to the Central Clutch soon.

katrina.name: Katrina
katrina.summary: One of the Order's youngest hoplites, whose heartbeast is the wolverine, the glutton: all but tireless, very strong and immune to cold. She serves the Quaesitores, travels with Adrasteia, and is preparing to challenge for archmage, exploring magical sites for creatures whose vis she can trade for items useful in either form.

mary.name: Mary
mary.summary: The senior maga of the Rorschach Chapter, a Gifted Mercere who makes lesser enchanted devices for Redcaps of other Tribunals: illusions for disguise, invisibility and swift travel.

rogitien.name: Rogitien
rogitien.summary: Of the Rorschach Chapter: an alchemist with the Gentle Gift who brews the longevity potions of the Tribunal's Redcaps and, by arrangement with House Guernicus, its long-serving hoplites. He prefers travel to the laboratory and goes often between the covenants. His large mundane family has many Redcaps in it.

pietro.name: Pietro
pietro.summary: Archmage of Juno's Spire, the Tribunal's senior hoplite and its lictor: a spry, small, elderly man fascinated by structured conflict. Trained in House Tytalus, he won his way into Flambeau by beating its champions with lightning, because it was hard and because some Tytalus think it their duty to found lineages in other Houses; some Flambeau call his descendants, the Jovians, interlopers. Hunting a leopard for his hoplite's sash, he was stalked and ambushed by it, and courted it as his familiar: Cinnamon, who catches birds from behind clouds. Rumour makes him the Antares, the Council of Archmagi's ceremonial war leader, who wears a great ruby.

jacinta.name: Jacinta
jacinta.summary: Archmaga of the Tower of Ashes, filia Nicoli of the line of Apromor: the eldest of her line and so the most able Perdo maga in the Order, who studies "suboptimal" spells that make Perdo do other Techniques' work (one ages blood into a scab to bind wounds, another destroys disease spirits; Carve the Mystic Tower etches a building out of rock). Many Alpine magi hope she dies before the few Flambeau older or deadlier than she, for as Prima she would make the Icy North her House's domus magna. She leads the Rowan Sisterhood. She and Pietro were born in the same Portuguese village, declared Wizard's War on each other on the same day twenty-eight years ago, and have been allies, rivals, enemies and perhaps lovers since; neither has fought a witnessed certamen. Her apprentice Ash is now the maga Noire.

yselt.name: Yselt
yselt.summary: Filia Rosalia, an ice-distorted, faerie-blooded maga who rarely leaves the covenant: leader of its council and community, a kind of stern aunt to her people, with the right to veto any policy. Her sigil is the icicle. Her sodales fear her Final Twilight may make her a faerie in the absent Queen's place, twisting the covenfolk into the shapes of the Queen's slain servants; she might one day have to be exiled. She and Andru of Valnastium are enemies, Miklos going between them.

carlo.name: Carlo
carlo.summary: Filius Innocu, born of two parents distorted by the Aura of Ice, with the barbegazi's features: huge feet to tunnel through snow or slide over ice, burial in snow no harm to him, blizzards at his call. No one can tell where his faerie powers end and his Hermetic magic begins; many think he makes gestures with his faerie powers as a private jest. His sigil is icicles forming in his beard.

charlotte.name: Charlotte
charlotte.summary: Filia Lupina, daughter of a farmer and a goose maiden, who lacks the bundle of feathers that would let her take her mother's shape: her master trimmed the few she sprouted each year and used them in experiments. Graduated a decade ago, she has saved every feather since as Muto vis, and does not know her bundle is almost whole. She is timid, happier in a group with a strong leader, and still stuck in the unhappy adolescence her master's meddling left her.

giselle.name: Giselle
giselle.summary: Filia Bertrand, taken as an apprentice in error: her father was no faerie but a water elemental that possessed and sustained a drowned sailor. She has Faerie Magic, but her style is practical, decisive and acquisitive, and she often represents the covenant to other magi: mysterious, a little frightening and skilled in certamen. Her sigil coats each spell's target in moisture, deadly in the Alps.

capra.name: Capra
capra.summary: Filia Bullfinch, a middle-aged Bjornaer maga whose heartbeast is the ibex. Faeries took her at sixteen, in mid-apprenticeship; she found her heartbeast with their help and served as a faerie wet nurse after her son, now the covenant's turb captain, was weaned. Recruited as a faerie midwife for the covenfolk's hard births, she travels the Order to deliver children too strange for Corpus spells. Her magic is poor for her age, and she cannot take an apprentice. She believes she is the new Amalthea, destined to find and raise the new Jupiter Pennius; her House thinks her mad and has asked the other Bjornaer to keep her from harm.

eginhard.name: Eginhard
eginhard.summary: Filius Caspar, of middle age, bonded with Kamilla; both take the shape of the lammergeier, and they share a laboratory and a sanctum. The less enlightened of the pair, since the perfect vulture is female, he spends more time in human form and has the better social skills: he dissects what he wants with great skill, mentions trouble-making stratagems to others rather than try them, and is glacially patient, then efficient and ruthless.

kamilla.name: Kamilla
kamilla.summary: Filia Bamber, slightly younger than her partner Eginhard and the dominant of the two: she exemplifies the vulture's mind, intimidating smaller creatures, endlessly patient and so prudent about combat that it passes for cowardice. (The book also spells her Kamillia.)

philomena.name: Philomena
philomena.summary: Archmaga, filia Rafe, the Longevity Project's chief researcher, slowed because her predecessors all but exhausted its line of work; if she succeeds, magi of middling Corpus could keep themselves until Twilight. Her own contribution is the potion that slows apparent aging. She asks magi to send her the bodies of human-shaped faeries through the Redcaps, freely shares a spell that keeps such bodies from decay, and pays for rare ones; some Merinita hate her for dissecting their kin. A Progressive, who sees Bonisagus as human and fallible and her own generation as no lesser. Many suspect she can strip a man's organs out onto a table; in truth she is no combat maga.

secrets.title: Philomena's faerie father
secrets.text: She is an amaranth halfling, daughter of one of the faeries who grow the forbidden flower: immune to it, since her body makes it, she stopped aging at 21 and began gaining Twilight as if under a longevity potion, and expects to fade into Arcadia to join her father.

secrets.title: Philomena and amaranth addicts
secrets.text: She has a weak hold over amaranth addicts, who resist her words the worse for their addiction.

paxon.name: Paxon
paxon.summary: Archmage, filius Valentin, the senior Verditius of the Tribunal and the finest longevity brewer active in the Order. He brews at most one potion for others every two years, and though a poor fighter has leverage enough to deter archmagi: to win his help one must outbid what an archmage or Primus could offer, and never by threat. He breaks no new ground and rarely competes at Verdi, so his House ranks him second tier, but he is its wealthiest and among its most influential. He holds the right to Staubbach Fall's Imaginem vis.

hubert.name: Hubert
hubert.summary: Filius Lorenz, who studies the means by which hedge wizards lengthen their lives, to give them Hermetic form. His best lead inverts a familiar bond, so that the magus dies of age only when his familiar does: a snake, an eagle or an immortal faerie or elemental would carry him to Twilight without aging rolls, but its death would kill him at once.

balbina.name: Balbina
balbina.summary: Filia Havelock (the member list calls her filius Seneca), whose name means stammerer: a curse stops her speaking aright while casting, so she leans on casting tools and is more traditional than most. She keeps the covenant's machines running, the great wheel above all, and is among the few of her House who repair enchanted items, a costly ritual designed anew each time; magi send her the strange things they dig up in the Levant, and she can often tell what one does and disable its defences. A descendant of Himinis the Mad, whose devices hide dangerous jokes.

sabastien.name: Sabastien
sabastien.summary: Filius Luise, a professional intruder: for a stiff fee he walks into a dead magus's sanctum, makes sure nothing is about to explode, and for more disarms its wards; diabolism costs extra. The Council of Archmagi and the Quaesitores hire him, and between jobs he breaks into living magi's labs to show them their weaknesses. One of the highest Parmas in the Order, a Rego Vim specialist who keeps his trade secrets, with Charmed Life or Destiny or both; he spreads rumours of a unique Parma, a way past the Aegis and an artifact of the Mercurian priesthood.

cara.name: Cara
cara.summary: Filia Sigurd, whose heartbeast is a piest, a serpent-whale the Irish know, from her birth near the Temple of Nodens in the Stonehenge Tribunal. She lives in the covenant's vast underground lake, explores the caves that riddle the Alps, and farms the deep pools: winkles by the pound and oysters by the bucket at the Fair, lobsters too big for two hands to ring, and now seed pearls, to ease the Tribunal's quarrel over wealth made by magic.

constance.name: Constance
constance.summary: Filia Frederich et Vortimer, over a hundred and thirty: trained in House Verditius, she worked for the Jerbiton under contract for fifty years before joining the House. Andru made her his Lesser Secundus, an office the Fifth Edition's House no longer has. A leader of the Craft School, which prizes the beautiful and the useful, she builds soaring, twisting laboratories and simple items for specialist labs; her lab texts sell at the Fair. Her adoptive parens Vortimer is of the lineage of Carolinus. The eldest living magus whose age the book gives, and so the Praeco here.

angela.name: Angela
angela.summary: Filia Constance, a Crafter who uses casting tools and makes magical instruments prized by musicians, and the covenant's factor at the Fair, where she buys unpredictably for her art, once a Belaquin grog's club of faerie-grown wood for its sound. Crafters and natural magicians compete for things of virtue. Not in the book's member list, but described as one (the twelfth).

sourdine.name: Sourdine
sourdine.summary: Filia Bronwyn, the House's finest spy: Gently Gifted and a silent caster of subtle gestures, she is Lord Roland of the Val Gardenia at the Emperor's court, but would sooner take a kidnapped servant's place and smooth it over with Mentem. One of Andru's closest confidants, she runs the top of his intelligence network, whose reports go to the library's correlators, and is Miklos's contact.

sirocco.name: Sirocco
sirocco.summary: Filia Andru, who leads the House's push into Islamic North Africa with the pro-Islamic Jerbiton of Iberia's "Roman" covenants and their links to Moorish magicians. She is quietly trying to learn what became of the last covenant founded near Tunis, said to be enslaved by desert demons.

grazia.name: Grazia
grazia.summary: Filia Natura, an Animal specialist who keeps the stables, kennels and mews: horses, donkeys, hounds and hawks trained to accept the Gifted, a few truly magical, sold at the Fair and along the Redcap roads. She pays well for breeding stock and established pairs of magical beasts, and is beginning to tame griffins.

kalliope.name: Kalliope
kalliope.summary: Filia Bibliophilus, a magus of middle years, the latest of the valley's line of librarian-magi, who keep a small community with their like at Durenmar, Verdi and a few other covenants.

bronwyn.name: Bronwyn
bronwyn.summary: Filia Astrolabe, trained by the Primus's own parens, who studies Hermetic phonotactics, the voice as a tool of casting, and now rhyme and metre in spells, which would make them easier to learn if harder to design. Flighty and easily distracted, she has not published, and her verse is doggerel.

carmine.name: Carmine
carmine.summary: Filia Susannah of House Flambeau, of mixed Iberian blood, one of the most beautiful women alive, dark-haired and dressed in black. She came in Andru's entourage forty-three years ago, became his model, his mistress and his wife, and is the valley's hostess. She follows the School of Sebastian, works magic on molten metal, and helps House Jerbiton when extreme violence is called for; she has passed the Jerbiton Gauntlet but prefers her independence. A muse. Their children are middle-aged, with grandchildren in their twenties; none has the Gift, and some are autocrats, scribes, priests and librarians (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 52).
